confirmed.title: The scene key must be the whole selection SET; a pinned scene page keeps the live members and drops the dead ones

PageFor: rebuild m_pinnedSel from the ALIVE subset (AddRange with primary = the first alive; if the old primary died, the next member becomes primary), return nullptr only when none survive. verdict.reason:
The UE citations say what is claimed. SDetailsView.cpp:609-628 `SetObjects` takes the whole `TArray<UObject*>` and the lock guards that array as a unit (`if (!IsLocked() || bOverrideLock)`). ObjectPropertyNode.cpp:117-133 `PurgeKilledObjects` iterates `Objects` and `RemoveCurrent()`s only the stale weak pointers, returning whether any were purged; SDetailsViewBase.cpp:1330-1336 calls it per root node on tick and :1394-1398 `ForceRefresh()`es over the survivors when `bDidPurgeObjects`. SDetailsView.cpp:852-856 flips `bIsLocked = false` only when `SelectedObjects.Num() == 0`. SLevelEditor.cpp:2228-2236 `OnElementSelectionChanged` refreshes every observing `SActorDetails` on any selection-set change. The mechanism (a locked/pinned view is keyed on the SET, drops dead members individually, empties only when nothing survives) is real.

The plan does not already handle it. Plan Task 3 Step 5 (plan lines 1254-1293): `KeyOf(Entity)` / `EntityOf(key)` are single-entity; `SelectionKey()` = `KeyOf(m_deps.selection->Primary())`; `PageFor` does `m_pinnedSel.Select(e)` (SelectionContext.hpp:36-40: `Select` = "selection becomes exactly { e }") and returns nullptr when that one entity is dead; `RestoreSelection` does `m_deps.selection->Select(e)`. Consequences confirmed against the real code: (1) the Inspector body is already multi-edit (EditorPanels.cpp:2549 iterates `sel.Entities()`, :2697 "fan-out targets", :2826 `targets = sel.Entities()`), so a pinned 3-entity page silently becomes a 1-entity page with no fan-out; (2) the LIVE selection survives member deaths because EditorAppFrame.cpp:3581 `m_selection.Prune(...)` drops only the dead ones and re-picks a primary (SelectionContext.hpp:82-90), but the PINNED page is rebuilt each frame from the primary alone and dies with it -- an asymmetry the UE mechanism removes; (3) back/forward `RestoreSelection` collapses a set to one entity.

One prong of the reviewer's argument is wrong and is dropped from the corrected change: `Toggle` (SelectionContext.hpp:44-58) makes a Ctrl-ADDED entity the primary, so the key changes and it IS an event; `AddRange` likewise sets the clicked row as primary. Only a Ctrl-REMOVE of a non-primary member (or a Prune of a non-primary member) keeps the key, which is a minor variant of the same defect. The reviewer's Breadcrumb item is already done: plan line 1303 reads `m_drawSel->Count()` for the "(+N)".

Not refuted on the other gates: the change keeps one window / one Inspector / sources / pages / pin / instances / history / task order; it changes only the scene source's opaque key format and its alive-subset rule; it copies a mechanism, no UE code; it is robustness (a pin that lies about what it pinned, a pin that dies while its members live), not taste. The proposed text was executable but imprecise on key order vs `SelectionContext`'s "front = oldest, primary = last-clicked" invariant and on where the test goes (Task 3 has no SceneInspectorSource test list; its only test is the DocumentHost observer case in Step 1), so `correctedChange` supplies the exact edits.
